data.claim: gate run aborts with a raw uncaught TimeoutError because the gate.started append raises TimeoutError when events.lock is held past lease.acquire_timeout_s, and run() has no handler for it
data.falsifier: A gate run whose gate.started append contends the lock for >30s would return a clean non-traceback result (or retry)
data.mechanism: run() appends gate.started via EventLog.append -> _flock -> fsio.file_lock(timeout=30s); on contention _flock raises builtin TimeoutError, run() has no try/except, outcome.exit_for(TimeoutError) has no declared exit so returns None -> cli re-raises a raw traceback
data.probe: Read ddflow/api/gates/_run.py run(), ddflow/infra/log/_lock.py _flock, ddflow/core/outcome.py exit_for
data.probe_output: run() calls log.append('gate.started') with no try/except; _flock raises TimeoutError after file_lock timeout; exit_for handles only KeyboardInterrupt+declared+ValueError/KeyError -> TimeoutError returns None
data.question: Why does ddflow gate run ci|unit_tests die with a raw traceback before the gate starts?

evidence.note: R5eb904a350 CONFIRMED: traced run() in ddflow/api/gates/_run.py -> log.append('gate.started') -> _flock raises TimeoutError after lease.acquire_timeout_s=30s; run() has no handler and outcome.exit_for(TimeoutError) returns None so the CLI re-raises a raw traceback. Falsifier (clean retry/result instead of traceback) addressed by _record_gate_started retry + clean O.nothing give-up.

ddflow brief --item read; r-gemini-key-load and r-task-phase-needs-wave reviewed; claim-then-edit followed (claimed before editing); regression test written before fix per bug rule; bug not closed without failing test.

commit a5c311e80: added _record_gate_started() + _GATE_START_LOCK_RETRY_S=300 in ddflow/api/gates/_run.py (retry events.lock for gate.started with visible stderr note, clean O.nothing exit-2 give-up) + regression test tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py; both inside declared globs after --add-globs ddflow/api/gates/_run.py.

chunk_findings.detail: `started_at = clock.now_iso()` is captured before the new retry loop, but `_record_gate_started` may succeed only after waiting on `events.lock` for minutes. The stale `started_at` is still the value passed to `_guarded`, so any timeout/deadline or duration computed from it includes the lock-wait time. For example, with a gate timeout of 300s and the events lock held for 200s, the command starts at t=200s but `_guarded` sees the run as already 200s old, leaving only about 100s of gate timeout (and the recorded start time is 200s before the actual start). The start timestamp should be captured after the successful `gate.started` append.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py (`started_at` capture before `_record_gate_started`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_record_gate_started` encodes success as `""` and failure as a non-empty string, returning `str(exc)` on timeout. If the timeout exception has no message (`TimeoutError()`, or a wrapper raising a bare `TimeoutError`), `str(exc)` is `""`; after the retry deadline the function returns `""`, so `run()` treats the failed append as success and proceeds to start the gate without a recorded `gate.started` event. A sentinel or explicit failure signal should be used instead of relying on the exception message being non-empty.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py (`_record_gate_started` uses `str(exc)` truthiness)

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test only exercises the “lock is already held at start” path: it holds `events.lock` externally, calls `_run.run`, and asserts the clean give-up result. It never exercises the complementary promise in the intent that “a long gate run should not hold the lock at start.” If `_record_gate_started`/`_run.run` were changed to acquire `events.lock` and retain it while the gate command runs, this test would still pass because the externally held lock forces the start-failure path and the assertions (`exit == 2`, reason, empty outcome, retry note) are exactly what that failure path produces. Thus a regression where the gate itself blocks other lanes’ heartbeats by holding `events.lock` during the run would not be caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: The new start-failure path returns after `_mark_or_refuse_twin` has already created/claimed the twin marker, but it never releases or unlinks that marker. For example, if `events.lock` remains held past `_GATE_START_LOCK_RETRY_S`, `_record_gate_started` returns a reason, `run` returns `O.nothing`, and the process continues with the twin marker still present; a later gate run for the same item/gate can then be refused as a twin even though no gate command ever started. The marker cleanup normally performed by `_guarded` is skipped on this new early-return path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py:452 (`run`, `_mark_or_refuse_twin` marker cleanup)

chunk_findings.detail: The new retry loop can wait up to 300 seconds after `_mark_or_refuse_twin(..., started_on, gdef.timeout_s)` has already created the twin marker. That marker’s timeout window is therefore consumed while the process is still trying to append `gate.started`. For example, with `gdef.timeout_s = 60` and `.ddflow/events.lock` held by another lane for 120 seconds, this run writes its twin marker at t=0 and retries until t=120. At t=70, another `ddflow gate run` can see the twin marker as expired/stale and start a second run; at t=120 the first run records `gate.started` and also starts, producing concurrent gate runs. The start retry should occur before the twin marker is created, or the marker should be refreshed and the twin revalidated after the wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py:452 (`run` retry after `_mark_or_refuse_twin`)

chunk_findings.detail: The first regression test does not actually verify that the gate command is not started when `_record_gate_started` fails. It configures the ci command as `echo ok`, but the assertions only check the returned exit code, reason, empty outcome, and retry note on stderr. If `_run.run` were changed to start the gate command before attempting to record the start event, the command would still run; a later failure to record `gate.started` could return the same `exit == 2` and reason, and the test would pass despite violating its stated goal that the run gives up “before its command starts.” The test needs a side-effect check (for example, a file written only by the command, or an assertion that the command output did not occur).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py:68

chunk_findings.detail: The gate command is constructed with an unquoted `sys.executable`. If the interpreter path contains spaces, such as `[REDACTED:path] Doe/.venv/bin/python`, the command string is split by the shell or by shell-like parsing, the gate command never starts, `began` is never written, and the test fails/timeouts. The executable should be quoted (e.g. via `shlex.quote(sys.executable)`) in the generated command.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py:78

data.probe: twin detection is pid-liveness: live_run -> _is_live -> alive(pid), not expected_s expiry; during the retry this run's pid is alive, so a second same-commit run is still refused as a twin (correct). expected_s is the watchdog's busy hint, not a twin expiry. Reordering twin AFTER gate.started would leave a dangling gate.started on twin refusal.

chunk_findings.detail: The second test never verifies that the `gate run` subprocess is still alive before it checks `events.lock`. It only waits for the gate command to create `began`; if `gate run` starts the command and then exits/crashes (or is otherwise terminated) before the lock check, any lock it held is released by process exit, so `_flock(..., 5)` succeeds and the test passes even though the code may have held `events.lock` until it exited. The test should assert `p.poll() is None` after `began.exists()` (and ideally re-check after the lock acquisition) to ensure it is actually measuring a running gate, as its comment claims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py:109

chunk_findings.detail: The new `cmd` builds a shell command by embedding `str(ran)!r` inside a double-quoted `-c` payload. If the pytest temp path contains a quote or shell-active character (for example, `TMPDIR=/tmp/it's`), the interpolated Python literal closes the outer double-quoted shell argument or is expanded before Python sees it. In that environment, even if a regression caused the gate command to start before `_record_gate_started` failed, the command would not create `ran`, so the new `assert not ran.exists()` at line 70 would pass vacuously. The test therefore no longer reliably proves that the command was not started when recording the start fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py:46

chunk_findings.detail: The retry bound is not enforced because the deadline is checked only before the 5-second sleep, not after it. If the remaining retry time is less than 5 seconds (for example, a regression test monkeypatches `_GATE_START_LOCK_RETRY_S` to 3 seconds and the first `log.append` raises `TimeoutError` after 2 seconds), the loop sleeps past `deadline` and issues another `log.append` attempt. If the lock has been released in the meantime, the function records `gate.started` after the declared bound; if the lock is still held, it blocks for another full acquire timeout before giving up. The loop should sleep only the remaining time or re-check the deadline after sleeping.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py:_record_gate_started

chunk_findings.detail: The first test claims to verify that `gate run` retries the held lock, but it only checks that the string `"waiting to record the run start"` appears once in stderr. An implementation that makes a single acquire attempt, prints that message, catches the timeout, and returns `exit == 2` with the expected reason would satisfy every assertion even though it never retried for `_GATE_START_LOCK_RETRY_S = 3.0`. Thus a regression that removes the retry loop or ignores the retry bound can pass this regression test; it needs to assert observable retry behavior (e.g. elapsed time near the bound or multiple retry notes).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py:71

chunk_findings.detail: The second test starts the gate run subprocess with `start_new_session=True` but cleans it up with `p.kill()`, which signals only the direct `ddflow` child. The configured gate command is a shell command (`touch began; sleep 30`), so the shell/sleep descendant can survive after the `finally` block and continue running for up to 30 seconds, keeping the subprocess’s pipe file descriptors open. Repeated test runs therefore leak processes; since the test deliberately creates a new session, cleanup should kill the process group (e.g. `os.killpg(os.getpgid(p.pid), signal.SIGKILL)`) rather than only the direct child.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_run_lock_retry.py:114

chunk_findings.detail: The retry bound can still be exceeded because the code rechecks `deadline` only before sleeping, then loops directly into another `log.append` attempt after the sleep. For example, with a 6-second retry bound and an events.lock acquisition that times out after 5 seconds, the first attempt fails at t=5, `remaining` is 1, the code sleeps 1 second, and then starts a second acquisition at t=6. If the lock is still held, that acquisition can take another 5 seconds, so the function does not return until about t=11; if the lock is released during that acquisition, it records `gate.started` after the declared bound. The previous fix capped the sleep duration but did not prevent this post-sleep attempt from overrunning the bound.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py:_record_gate_started
